newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bonfire of cigarettes to mark Iran's anti-U.S. day.
newsitem.headline: Bonfire of cigarettes to mark Iran's anti-U.S. day.

text.p: Iran will burn 10 million mostly U.S.-made cigarettes seized from smugglers as part of events on Sunday marking the 17th anniversary of the seizure of the United States embassy in Tehran, an Iranian newspaper said on Thursday.

The daily Akhbar quoted state tobacco official Hassan Fathi as saying the cigarettes, which did not meet Iranian standards or were damaged in transport, would be burned during events marking the seizure of the embassy by Moslem militants who held 52 Americans hostage for 444 days.

Several state bodies, including the Revolutionary Guards, on Thursday called on Iranians to attend nationwide rallies marking the day named "International Day of Struggle against World Arrogance", Tehran radio reported.

The main event is a march to the former embassy, dubbed "Den of Spies" by the late spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini. The ayatollah led the 1979 Islamic revolution which toppled the late Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, a close U.S. ally.
Fathi told the newspaper that an unspecified quantity of the seized cigarettes was fit for consumption and would be sold.
American cigarettes are widely available in Iran, where officials have said that up to 75 percent of the daily consumption of 150 million cigarettes is contraband.
Washington broke diplomatic ties with Tehran in 1980 during the hostage crisis.

The United States imposed a trade and investment ban on Iran last year, accusing it of sponsoring terrorism and seeking to develop nuclear weapons. Iran denies the charges and says the United States is bent on destroying the Islamic government.
